points.text: Lilly's triple agonist retatrutide beat Novo's Ozempic on blood sugar and weight loss in an 80-week head-to-head phase 3 diabetes trial, though with more side effects at the top dose.
Genmab's bispecific petosemtamab plus Keytruda significantly improved survival in first-line head and neck cancer, an early payoff for its $8B Merus buyout.

US regulators moved in two directions: FDA set out a route to approve gene editing therapies made for single patients, while HHS let pharmacies compound six unproven wellness peptides without FDA review.
China approved Bayer's asundexian for secondary stroke prevention, the first approval for a Factor XIa blood thinner.
Biosecurity: Nature says a possible plague lab leak in Russia shows global oversight gaps, and an mRNA vaccine protected dairy cows from H5N1 bird flu.
Biomanufacturing: Formo and Those Vegan Cowboys won FDA GRAS clearance for animal-free casein, and Biosphere got a $21M Pentagon contract to bio-produce critical chemicals.

8eccb6629bd1.summary: STAT examines why US overdose deaths fell 27% in 2024, with preliminary 2025 data showing another significant drop.

healthcare.why: Public health trend with policy implications.

7b1b9de47181.summary: Geron is discontinuing its phase 3 IMpactMF trial of imetelstat in relapsed or refractory myelofibrosis.

pharma.why: Ends a key label-expansion hope for Geron's only drug.

investment.why: Material setback for a commercial-stage biotech.

dcd9344ca6d8.summary: Scipher Medicine launched PrismTcell, a molecular test to predict response to abatacept in rheumatoid arthritis; it says patients selected with it had about twice the ACR50 response rate.

f36b8e7e51e7.summary: electroCore filed a 510(k) asking FDA to clear its Quell device for chemotherapy-induced neuropathy, citing about 40% lower pain scores in two studies of 168 people.

meddevices.why: Neuromodulation device seeking a new indication.

96ccf36345d3.summary: Blue Lake Biotechnology received a $5 million grant to expand its paediatric phase 1/2a trial of intranasal RSV vaccine BLB201 and study transmission.

pharma.why: Non-dilutive funding for a vaccine programme.

d3321d906833.summary: Canada's Department of National Defence awarded SIGA a contract worth up to $15 million for smallpox antiviral TPOXX.

biosecurity.why: Smallpox countermeasure stockpiling.

5a4fde4194c6.summary: Mineralys says phase 2 Explore-CKD results, published in Kidney International, showed lorundrostat added to an SGLT2 inhibitor significantly lowered systolic blood pressure at four weeks.

pharma.why: Supports an aldosterone synthase inhibitor in kidney disease.

10fd18524d55.summary: Amatera combines automated high-throughput plant cell culture with machine learning to speed development of new crop varieties.

08b2f3e106c6.summary: Labiotech reviews the race to develop TROP2-targeting antibody-drug conjugates in cancer.

pharma.why: Competitive ADC landscape.

8be558fde76b.summary: Israeli food tech Meala entered full-scale production of texturising pea proteins at two European sites, able to replace 1,400 tonnes of eggs a year.

508f8daa3341.summary: A machine learning 'digital twin' trained on single-cell protein profiles predicted immune responses to drug candidates meant to delay preterm labour.

ai.why: AI model for drug response prediction.

3921f21fb389.summary: The Scientist reports researchers and drug developers remain divided on whether GLP-1 drugs could extend lifespan.

pharma.why: Possible longevity indication for GLP-1s.

a4696d32ebcc.summary: In a clinical trial, a daily fibre supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain, improved muscle strength and lowered pain sensitivity.

285b56195fde.summary: Junshi says final analysis of the phase 3 NEOTORCH study showed perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy durably improved event-free and overall survival in resectable stage II-III lung cancer.

pharma.why: Survival data for a Chinese PD-1 in early lung cancer.

565bceb71406.summary: US startup BMC Ingredients won Indian FSSAI approval for its Rhiza mycoprotein and plans to launch in India in Q2 2027.

fermentation.why: Regulatory approval for a fermentation-derived protein.

agrifood.why: Entry to India's large protein market.

9ebb265c4e13.summary: Nature Biotechnology paper describes smCRISPRa, an engineered compact Cas12m system for efficient multiplexed gene activation in mice.

pharma.why: Compact enough for in vivo delivery of gene activation therapies.

ac29eaea7d3d.summary: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine protected lactating dairy cows from H5N1 bird flu infection, according to a Nature Biotechnology paper.

agrifood.why: Potential tool to control H5N1 in US dairy herds.

biosecurity.why: Reduces a key reservoir for pandemic flu risk.

healthcare.why: Lower spillover risk to farm workers.

bef6e2ae25be.summary: Preprint: directed evolution produced enzymes that degrade several types of plastic. Not yet peer-reviewed.

989b479652d7.summary: Preprint: CAR-macrophages targeting fibroblast-like synoviocytes eased inflammatory and degenerative arthritis in models. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Cell therapy approach for arthritis.

8b2f26f73613.summary: Preprint: an engineered compact TnpB nuclease, ISPmu1, delivered with donor DNA in a single AAV achieved targeted genome integration in vivo. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Compact editor for in vivo gene insertion.

4c41f455fb1b.summary: Heart muscle channels lactate directly into mitochondria via MCT1 to make energy, challenging the prevailing view of lactate metabolism, a Nature study reports.

pharma.why: New metabolic target in heart disease.

1c75d691087b.summary: A controlled human infection study shows how preexisting antibodies shape dengue replication and immune responses on reinfection, including in vaccinated people, informing safer vaccines against all four strains.

pharma.why: Guides next-generation dengue vaccines.

8b3f10438211.summary: Researchers found a previously unknown role for a cell-cycle enzyme in starting cell proliferation, which may explain toxic effects of its inhibitors.

pharma.why: Could inform safety of cell-cycle inhibitor drugs.

6532dd2d14ec.summary: Aberrant splicing in neutrophils creates new peptides that T and B cells recognise in lupus, a Nature study finds.

pharma.why: New antigen targets in lupus.

b910df45d987.summary: Phase 1 of the TenK10K project combined single-cell RNA sequencing and whole-genome sequencing from 1,925 people to link rare and common variants to immune cell gene expression.

pharma.why: Helps prioritise immune drug targets.

6c979cf445f5.summary: Tumour assembloids combining kidney cancer cells, fibroblasts and T cells reproduce tumour-immune crosstalk in the lab.

pharma.why: Better preclinical model for immunotherapy testing.

56e354d7753e.summary: A multi-ancestry Alzheimer's genetics study identifies new risk loci and potential drug targets in microglia and neurons.

pharma.why: New Alzheimer's drug target candidates.

0fb08c76b70e.summary: Single-cell chromatin profiling links non-coding genetic variants to disease risk in specific cell types and states.

pharma.why: Target identification.

6748d82f10da.summary: Drug inhibition of the m7G methyltransferase METTL1 slowed tumour growth and prolonged survival in several mouse models of solid and blood cancers.

pharma.why: Preclinical validation of an RNA-modification cancer target.

063b26b5dfe0.summary: Preprint: an anchoring nanobody loads biologics onto circulating extracellular vesicles in the body and redirects them to tissues. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Possible new drug delivery route.

14a710dfb1e7.summary: BioProcess International looks at the path towards autonomous bioprocess control.

bac72534b4a0.summary: NEJM trial compares IVF with intrauterine insemination for couples with unexplained infertility.

71f04320c56c.summary: Preprint: computationally designed de novo protein minibinders target specific sites on cancer target STAT3. Not yet peer-reviewed.

ai.why: Computational protein design for hard targets.

pharma.why: Alternative to failed small-molecule STAT3 drugs.

37c8eb604561.summary: Preprint: a bivalent Lassa virus mRNA vaccine protected guinea pigs from lethal infection. Not yet peer-reviewed.

biosecurity.why: No licensed Lassa vaccine exists yet.

pharma.why: mRNA vaccine for a priority pathogen.

f7ae9c7070ec.summary: The UK MHRA opened a consultation on indefinitely recognising CE-marked medical devices in Great Britain.

meddevices.why: Decides UK market access for EU-certified devices.

23ad0624e77c.summary: Nature Biotechnology paper repurposes engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing.

pharma.why: Human-derived RNA editor may lower immunogenicity.

extra.title: Japan's Astellas Pharma inks $400M deal with AI Proteins to develop miniprotein therapeutics
extra.summary: Astellas signed a research collaboration and licence agreement with US computational protein design company AI Proteins, which is eligible for more than $400 million in upfront and milestone payments plus royalties. AI Proteins will design miniproteins against several targets and Astellas takes an exclusive worldwide licence to the candidates.

ai.why: De novo computational protein design backed by a large pharma deal.

pharma.why: Japanese pharma buys into a new therapeutic modality.

investment.why: $400M+ in potential payments for a private AI biotech.

extra.title: Singapore launches national reference to guide clinical investigations of medical devices
extra.summary: Singapore published Technical Reference TR 151:2026 on clinical investigation of medical devices, setting out what a device study application should contain and how to apply ISO 14155:2026 locally. It is meant to make ethics review more predictable, since most existing trial guidance was written for medicines.

meddevices.why: Clear national rules for running device trials in Singapore.

diagnostics.why: Applies to diagnostic devices studied clinically.

extra.title: Singapore's biopharma manufacturers launch S$4.8M study award for manufacturing careers
extra.summary: The Biopharmaceutical Manufacturers' Advisory Council launched a S$4.8 million study award expected to reach about 1,000 polytechnic and ITE students over five years, with cash awards of S$3,000-5,000 and priority internships at member companies.

bioprocessing.why: Workforce pipeline for biopharma manufacturing in a major hub.

pharma.why: Industry investment in local skills.

extra.title: Samsung Bioepis targets 20 biosimilars by 2030, eyes ADC and obesity drugs
extra.summary: Samsung Bioepis plans to grow from 11 marketed biosimilars to 20 by 2030 and is eyeing ADCs and obesity drugs; it filed in Korea in August for SB27, a Keytruda biosimilar.

pharma.why: Biosimilar pipeline targets originals with about 114 trillion won in 2025 sales, including Keytruda.

bioprocessing.why: Expansion by one of the largest biologics manufacturing groups.

extra.title: ECDC update: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, multi-country, 2026
extra.summary: ECDC updated its tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak on 26 October: DRC had reported 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 related deaths across eight provinces by 18 October, and Nigeria reported a case on 20 October in a traveller from Uganda, with 53 contacts identified.

biosecurity.why: Large Ebola outbreak now with exported cases in Nigeria and Kenya.

healthcare.why: Major public health emergency in Africa with imported-case risk elsewhere.

pharma.why: No licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo virus; trials are under way.

diagnostics.why: Need for testing at borders and in affected countries.

extra.title: Kaigene signs agreement worth up to $580M with Korea's Celltrion for anti-APRIL antibody KG013
extra.summary: Celltrion took exclusive worldwide rights to Kaigene's half-life-extended anti-APRIL antibody KG013, initially for IgA nephropathy; Kaigene is eligible for up to $580.5 million including an undisclosed upfront and milestones, plus royalties.

pharma.why: Korean biologics giant buys into a novel antibody for a hot kidney disease target.

investment.why: Up to $580M deal for a US biotech.

extra.title: Waters and Labcorp to expand access to cervical cancer screening
extra.summary: Labcorp and Waters will offer the FDA-approved BD Onclarity HPV assay, which separately identifies six high-risk HPV types, through Labcorp's US network from late 2026, including its consumer channel.

diagnostics.why: Extended HPV genotyping rolled out by a national lab.

healthcare.why: Aims to close the US cervical screening gap.

extra.title: Enhertu approved in the EU as adjuvant treatment for patients with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment for HER2-positive early breast cancer
extra.summary: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu for HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment. AstraZeneca says in the DESTINY-Breast05 phase 3 trial it cut the risk of invasive recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 (3-year IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%).

pharma.why: Moves a leading ADC into the curative early-disease setting in Europe.

healthcare.why: Changes standard care for high-risk early breast cancer patients.

extra.title: Korea's biohealth exports hit record $24.8 billion as cosmetics surge 31%
extra.summary: South Korea's biohealth exports rose 19.4% to a record $24.75B in the first nine months of 2026, per KHIDI; pharmaceuticals grew 14.2% to $8.93B, led by biopharmaceuticals at $5.71B, while pharma exports to the US fell 30%.

pharma.why: Korean biologics and biosimilar exports keep growing.

bioprocessing.why: Reflects Korea's CDMO and biosimilar manufacturing scale.

extra.title: Asundexian first Factor XIa inhibitor approved in China for stroke risk reduction after priority review
extra.summary: China approved Bayer's once-daily asundexian (Sunharbo) to reduce stroke risk after non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or high-risk TIA, the first approval for a Factor XIa inhibitor; Bayer says it cut ischaemic stroke by 26% without more bleeding in the 12,327-patient OCEANIC-STROKE trial.

pharma.why: First-ever approval for the Factor XIa class of blood thinners.

healthcare.why: New secondary stroke prevention option without added bleeding.

investment.why: Key growth asset for Bayer; other filings under review.

extra.title: Korea to Nurture 200 Pharma and Biotech Ventures by 2030
extra.summary: South Korea's health and SME ministries launched the K-Pharma-Bio Frontier Company programme, selecting 50 ventures a year to reach 200 by 2030, with 60 billion won of investment and 90 billion won of guarantees over three years.

investment.why: State capital and guarantees for Korean biotech startups.

pharma.why: 40% of slots go to new drug developers.

meddevices.why: 20 slots for digital health and device firms.

bioprocessing.why: 10 slots for biomaterials and production technology.
